observations.text: RSMeM FAM retrieval is deterministic and instance-indexed: for instance i, the latest reflection from M_i is retrieved. Public code mirrors this with question_id-indexed get_latest_reflection and same-question injection. The design avoids interference from unrelated failure patterns by not doing cross-instance semantic FAM transfer.

FAR-only component evidence is science-domain and matched at the component level: on Qwen3-8B, baseline outcome accuracy 31.98 rises to 39.68 with FAR; on DeepSeek-V3.2, 48.18 rises to 53.44 with FAR. FAR disables HKG, while baseline disables both HKG and FAR. FAR also changes retry/reflection machinery, so this is component evidence rather than a perfect single-bit intervention.

The summary_ftro reflection implementation writes compact retry reflections while separately persisting provenance sidecars keyed by question_id and hashes: full_trajectory_sha256, ftro_sha256, and prompt_sha256. Cached reuse is conditional on matching trajectory hashes.

protocol_inferences.name: EXACT_SCOPE_KEY_FOR_RETRY_MEMORY
protocol_inferences.text: For retry memory whose intended scope is one execution instance, exact target identity is itself a strong applicability gate; do not broaden to cross-target reuse without a separate requalification step.

protocol_inferences.name: BOUNDED_OPERATIONAL_MEMORY_WITH_PROVENANCE_SIDECAR
protocol_inferences.text: A handoff/retry payload can remain compact while binding to immutable sidecar evidence carrying source trajectory/prompt hashes. Bounded context and replay/audit provenance are compatible rather than competing goals.

causal_boundary: RSMeM directly supports failure-derived memory for same-instance retries. It does not test cross-target receiver-side applicability/revalidation while holding stored memory and retrieval fixed.
next_probe: Search for a science-domain intervention that reuses a failure record across targets and ablates only target-side applicability/revalidation.
